title: AI Companies Are Trying to Hide a Staggering Amount of Debt
titleZh: 人工智能公司正试图隐藏巨额债务
author: technewssss
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Illustration by Tag Hartman-Simkins / Futurism. Source: Shutterstock Sign up to see the future, today Can’t-miss innovations from the bleeding edge of science and tech
AI companies are pouring untold billions of dollars into enormous data centers in their efforts to sustain increasingly complex and resource-intensive AI models.

It’s an extremely costly undertaking built on seemingly bottomless hype — and a mountain of debt. As Japanese financial newspaper Nikkei Asia found in a recent investigation, just five US tech giants — Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Oracle — are hiding an estimated $1.65 trillion in debt that doesn’t appear on balance sheets. That’s even more than the $1.35 trillion in debt the five companies officially reported in their financial data for the most recent quarter.

Meta alone has amassed around $420 billion in off-balance-sheet debt, according to Nikkei, highlighting how precarious the AI industry’s steep investment in AI has become, and inspiring comparisons to energy company Enron, which collapsed in spectacular fashion in 2001 because of similar debts hidden behind shell companies. Like Enron, they’re using special purpose vehicles, or off-balance sheet arrangements such as legally distinct subsidiaries, as a way to make their financial reporting look healthier than it actually is — often a glaring sign that something is deeply amiss behind the scenes.

“The accounting treatment itself is in fashion,” technical accounting consultant Tom Selling told Bloomberg. “But what if one of these companies was a house of cards and was propping itself up with this accounting treatment? To me, that’s the risk.”

children.author: hualapais
children.textRawHtml:
I suggest looking into “EQL”, or better yet, just replicating its index by taking a position in the 11 XL* sector funds from SPDR, allocating equal weighting to each. One will end up with one’s equities equal weighted by sector and with plenty of large cap exposure, as opposed to the pronounced mid-cap tilt found in whole market equal-weight strategies.

Personally, I drop the financial sector entirely (Thomistic prohibitions on usury) which leaves an even 10 funds which is easy to allocate mentally and in practice. For example, assuming a 60/40 allocation where one is holding the lion’s share in equities and the remainder in bonds (I substitute with a combination of gold, crypto, cash, and Swiss Franc here), one would allocate as follows:

XLC 6% XLY 6% XLP 6% XLE 6% XLV 6% XLI 6% XLB 6% XLK 6% XLU 6% XLRE 6%

(Note that XLF is consciously not taken as a position here, decide if it’s right for you. The Mortgate REITs which would make XLRE problematic are in XLF per the sector selection rules)

The remaining 40% is bonded debt if you are fine with usury, or some sort of asset negatively or neutrally correlated to equities.

children.author: rocho
children.textRawHtml: Why do you consider bonds usury?

children.author: hualapais
children.textRawHtml:
Because bonds involve interest. Per Summa Theologica:

> To take usury for money lent is unjust in itself, because this is to sell what does not exist, and this evidently leads to inequality which is contrary to justice.

https://www.newadvent.org/summa/3078.htm

…Aquinas expands the analysis but it is relatively straightforward: all interest is usury.

Personally, I find it helpful to imagine two hypothetical persons representing the entire economy, one the creditor who is lending and two the borrower who is taking on the loan. In this ultra simple closed model with a fixed quantity of money, the former is in effect asking for more units of money than actually exist in the whole system. When the loan comes due the borrower owes a sum that cannot be paid in full from the circulating medium itself. Settlement then requires either default, the creditor forgiving the excess, or the transfer of real goods and property to make up the difference. Scaled up, that same pressure (the continuous generation of monetary claims that exceed the existing stock of money) is what I suspect drives a good deal of the subtle and overt strain on families and communities that people so often complain of in the West and in modern growth-oriented capital societies.

This definition of usury differs from the modern loophole-definition: that interest bearing loans are only usury when the rates cross some nebulous abusive threshold. In the above Thomistic interpretation, all interest is socially problematic and disfavored. Judaism holds to a similar prohibition on interest when loans are made between Jews. Islam likewise prohibit usury even more broadly. Despite the injunction against usury in the Middle Ages Christendom and the enduring prohibitions of usury in other faiths, there are many modern Catholics and Protestants who will favor the modern interpretation over Thomas’ understanding; I’m just not one of them.
children.textZhHtml:
因为债券涉及利息。 《神学大全》：

>借出的钱拿高利贷本身就是不公正的，因为这是出售不存在的东西，这显然会导致违背正义的不平等。

https://www.newadvent.org/summa/3078.htm

……阿奎那扩展了分析，但相对简单：所有利息都是高利贷。

就个人而言，我发现想象两个代表整个经济的假设人是有帮助的，一个是放贷的债权人，两个是接受贷款的借款人。在这个具有固定货币数量的超简单封闭模型中，前者实际上要求比整个系统中实际存在的货币单位更多的货币单位。当贷款到期时，借款人欠下一笔无法从流通媒介本身全额支付的款项。然后，和解需要违约、债权人宽恕超额部分，或者转移实际货物和财产来弥补差额。扩大规模后，我怀疑同样的压力（超过现有货币存量的货币债权的不断产生）给家庭和社区带来了很多微妙和明显的压力，而在西方和现代增长导向的资本社会中，人们经常抱怨这种压力。

这种高利贷的定义与现代漏洞定义不同：只有当利率超过某个模糊的滥用门槛时，计息贷款才算高利贷。在上述托马斯主义的解释中，所有的利益都是社会问题和不受欢迎的。当犹太人之间借贷时，犹太教也有类似的利息禁令。 伊斯兰教同样更广泛地禁止高利贷。 尽管中世纪基督教世界禁止高利贷，其他宗教也长期禁止高利贷，但仍有许多现代天主教徒和新教徒更倾向于现代解释而不是托马斯的理解。我只是不是他们中的一员。

children.author: hualapais
children.textRawHtml:
The opportunity cost point is fair enough if one is thinking in terms of two concrete individuals. The illustration I offered was meant at a more abstract level, the two persons standing in for the creditor side and the debtor side of a closed economy taken as wholes. In that framing the issue is not whether a particular borrower can put the money to productive use (clearly he can), but that the system as a whole is being asked to generate more units of the circulating medium than currently exist within it. Even when real value is created, the monetary claim still exceeds the monetary stock. Settlement then requires continuous expansion of the money supply, continuous transfer of existing assets toward creditors, or periodic default. That structural pressure is what I was trying to get at.

I suspect the deeper difficulty is the “bond” in bonds themselves, the ongoing compulsion that interest introduces. Once interest is attached the debtor is under continuous obligation to produce additional claims simply to keep the accounts from breaking. Traditional writers on the Christian and Islamic sides generally preferred arrangements that avoided this continuous pressure. A pure discount (as with discounted Treasury bills and similar instruments) prices the time element once, up front: the creditor advances a smaller sum and later receives the larger face amount. The cost is paid at the beginning rather than levied as a recurring claim that must be met out of future circulation. In that sense the time value is acknowledged without the mechanism that forces the system to keep generating more monetary units than presently exist.

[edit:] Clarified the discount language.
children.textZhHtml:
如果一个人从两个具体个体的角度思考，机会成本点就足够公平了。我提供的例子是在更抽象的层面上，两个人代表封闭经济体的债权人和债务人。在这个框架中，问题不在于特定借款人是否可以将资金用于生产性用途（显然他可以），而在于整个系统被要求生成比当前存在的更多的流通媒介单位。即使创造了实际价值，货币债权仍然超过货币存量。然后，结算需要不断扩大货币供应量，不断将现有资产转移给债权人，或者定期违约。这种结构性压力正是我想要表达的。

我怀疑更深层次的困难在于债券本身的“债券”，即利息带来的持续强迫。一旦附加利息，债务人就有持续义务提出额外的债权，只是为了防止账目破裂。基督教和伊斯兰教方面的传统作家通常更喜欢避免这种持续压力的安排。纯粹的贴现（与贴现的国库券和类似工具一样）预先对时间要素进行一次定价：债权人预付较小的金额，然后收到较大的票面金额。该费用是在开始时支付的，而不是作为必须在未来流通中满足的经常性索赔来征收。从这个意义上说，时间价值是在没有强制系统继续产生比目前存在的更多货币单位的机制的情况下得到承认的。

children.author: hiAndrewQuinn
children.textRawHtml:
This still seems off to me. If I were a potential creditor in such a closed loop system, and I was told I absolutely could not charge interest due to these monetary supply constraints, I would either just stop lending entirely or I would demand something that isn't strictly denominated in money to make the risk I'm taking on, etc worth my capital outlay.

But then eventually, if the system were sufficiently complex, I'd probably tire of whatever complicated barter system we have already going on, and then it's likely some third party would step in offering something that's totally not money, dude, trust me, it's just like a handy clearinghouse of IOUs for people engaged in the trade of these non-monetary favors for favors...

Some people who hold or offer such IOUs might then take the bold step of calling them non-exclusive, as in I will mow the lawn of whoever happens to have my "one lawn mowed" voucher, I just happened to originally give it to this first guy, I have no idea what he did with it after that... Other people realize this "non exclusivity" deal actually makes the voucher strictly more valuable, you can do more things with it than you could otherwise... You see where I'm going with this. It's not passing my sniff test.
children.textZhHtml:
我仍然觉得这很奇怪。如果我是这样一个闭环系统中的潜在债权人，并且我被告知由于这些货币供应限制我绝对不能收取利息，我要么完全停止放贷，要么我会要求一些不严格以货币计价的东西来使我所承担的风险等值得我的资本支出。

但最终，如果系统足够复杂，我可能会厌倦我们已经进行的任何复杂的易货系统，然后很可能一些第三方会介入提供一些东西这完全不是钱，伙计，相信我，它就像一个方便的借条票据交换所，供那些从事这些非货币恩惠交易的人使用。

一些持有或提供此类借条的人可能会采取大胆的步骤，称它们为非排他性，就像在“我将为碰巧拥有我的“割过一次草坪”凭证的人修剪草坪一样，我只是碰巧最初把它给了这个第一个伙计，我不知道他之后用它做了什么......其他人意识到这种“非排他性”交易实际上使优惠券更有价值，你可以用它做比其他方式更多的事情......你知道我要做什么。它没有通过我的嗅探测试。

children.author: geye1234
children.textRawHtml:
Greetings, fellow Thomist. You are correct that usury is any amount of interest, and attempts to pretend otherwise are sophistical, but I suggest you may want to look again at corporate bonds and other non-recourse loans -- that is, loan where collateral is limited to specified asset(s). Look at Zippy Catholic's writing on the subject -- he was a finance dude, and a very rich self-made man. A non-recourse loan is more like taking an ownership share in something, and then renting it back. It's unfortunate that we use the same words (loan, interest, debt) for both full-recourse and non-recourse contracts, because they're entirely different things.

I agree that charging interest on a full-recourse loan is a wicked and disgusting thing to do to one's fellow man, and I'd say it's in the same genus as slavery. Usury is to fraud what robbery is to larceny. It's also interesting that the markets where usury is most prevalent (housing, college fees) are the ones that have seen the most insane price increases.
children.textZhHtml:
你好，托马斯同胞。您说的高利贷是任何金额的利息，这是正确的，并且试图假装不这样做是很狡猾的，但我建议您可能想再次看看公司债券和其他无追索权贷款——即抵押品仅限于指定资产的贷款。看看齐皮·天主教徒（Zippy Catholic）关于这个主题的文章——他是一位金融人士，也是一位白手起家的非常富有的人。无追索权贷款更像是获得某物的所有权份额，然后将其租回。不幸的是，我们对完全追索权合同和无追索权合同使用相同的词（贷款、利息、债务），因为它们是完全不同的东西。

我同意对完全追索权贷款收取利息对同胞来说是一件邪恶而令人厌恶的事情，我想说这与奴隶制属于同一类。高利贷之于诈骗，正如抢劫之于盗窃。同样有趣的是，高利贷最盛行的市场（住房、大学学费）也是价格上涨最疯狂的市场。

children.author: michaelt
children.textRawHtml:
In many historical societies, religious prohibitions on usury meant the charging of interest of any kind.

Jump in a time machine to 1515 and ask Martin Luther, or to 1260 and ask Thomas Aquinas, they'd tell you it's sinful.

And in the present age, a fair number of Islamic folk consider interest against their religion's rules. So there's a Halal finance industry where, for example, you can get a "murabahah contract" where the bank buys a house, then sells the house to you at a higher price, while allowing you to pay them in monthly instalments.
children.textZhHtml:
在许多历史社会中，宗教禁止高利贷意味着收取任何形式的利息。

乘坐时光机到 1515 年问马丁·路德，或者到 1260 年问托马斯·阿奎那，他们会告诉你这是有罪的。

在当今时代，相当多的伊斯兰教徒认为利息违反了他们的宗教规则。因此，存在清真金融行业，例如，您可以获得“murabahah 合同”，银行购买房屋，然后以更高的价格将房屋卖给您，同时允许您按月分期付款。
